ORC — time-on-distance rounds each allowance product, against the fastest boat that finished

ORC Rating Systems 403.2: CT = ET − ToD × distance + ToD of the scratch boat × distance, rounded to the second (401.2). ORC Scorer rounds each product to the second and subtracts, as ORC's PCS module does for 402.9, and takes the scratch boat from the boats that finished.

Scoring system: ORC 
APHD allowances in s/NM, a 4.37 NM course, start 15:00:00:
  Kestrel  548.2 — the fastest rating, but retires
  Mojo     594.7 — the fastest-rated boat that finished: the scratch boat
  Ruffian  620.0

The scratch boat is Mojo, not Kestrel: a boat that didn't finish isn't the
boat the fleet is corrected against. Mojo's corrected time is its elapsed
time. (With Kestrel as scratch every corrected time would fall by the same
203 s and the order would be the same; it's the published figure that
changes.)

Each product is rounded to the second before subtracting:
  Mojo:    594.7 × 4.37 = 2598.839 → 2599
  Ruffian: 620.0 × 4.37 = 2709.4   → 2709

  Mojo:    finish 15:46:20  ET 2780  CT = 2780 − 2599 + 2599 = 2780
  Ruffian: finish 15:48:10  ET 2890  CT = 2890 − 2709 + 2599 = 2780

They tie, sharing (1 + 2) / 2 = 1.5 points. Rounding the difference once
instead would give Ruffian 2890 − 110.561 = 2779.439 → 2779, and the race
outright.
